e.etymology: Two names in one spelling: Welsh eira, the everyday word for snow, and a Scandinavian and Finnish name from Eir, the Old Norse goddess of healing, whose name means 'relief, mercy'.
An -ah spelling of Amora, a modern name built on amor, the Spanish and Latin word for love.

From an English surname, either from darnel, a kind of ryegrass, or from the place Darnall in Yorkshire, Old English derne, 'hidden', plus halh, 'nook'. It rose as an American first name in the mid-20th century.
A spelling of Bridget with the French-looking -ette ending. Bridget is the English form of Irish Brighid, 'exalted one', the name of a Celtic goddess and of Saint Brigid of Kildare.
From Latin terra, 'earth, land', also the name of the Roman earth goddess. American parents took it up in the 1970s, when it sat close to Tara and Sierra.

assoc.t: Terra, the earth-moving hero of Teen Titans

e.etymology: A modern spelling of Micah, the Hebrew prophet's name meaning 'who is like Yahweh?', used mostly for girls. Some families say it like Mika.
From an English surname, a variant of Trewhitt, taken from a place in Northumberland. The spelling Truett is better known through Chick-fil-A founder S. Truett Cathy.
A recent American name with the sound of the Hawaiian names Kalani and Leilani and of Delaney. It has no established meaning of its own.
From Arabic misk, 'musk', the costly perfume; the Quran describes the drink of paradise as sealed with musk. It has become a fashionable girls' name in the Arab world.
The French form of Diana, the Roman goddess of the hunt and the moon, whose name comes from an old root meaning divine or shining. It was highly popular in the United States in the 1940s and 1950s.

assoc.t: Jack & Diane, John Mellencamp's 1982 hit song

e.etymology: A short form of Jedidiah, Hebrew for 'beloved of Yahweh', the name the prophet Nathan gave to the infant Solomon.
namesakes: Jed Clampett (patriarch of The Beverly Hillbillies)
Jed Bartlet (the president on The West Wing)

assoc.t: Jed Clampett of The Beverly Hillbillies

e.meaning: son of Coinneach, the handsome one
e.etymology: A short form of Mackenzie used on its own. Mackenzie is the Scottish surname Mac Coinnich, 'son of Coinneach', a Gaelic name meaning comely or handsome.
The Polish form of Sophia, from Greek sophia, 'wisdom'. It has been one of the most popular girls' names in Poland for centuries, with the pet form Zosia.
A modern American blend of Ray or Rae with the -lin ending, one of several spellings alongside Raelynn and Raylen.
A respelling of Colby, an English surname from villages in Norfolk and Cumbria. The place name joins the Old Norse personal name Koli to byr, 'farm, settlement'.

assoc.t: Colby, a mild orange American cheese (sounds the same)

e.etymology: A spelling of Jenny, originally a pet form of Jane and Janet, which go back to Hebrew Yochanan, 'God is gracious'; later it also served for Jennifer. Jennie was the usual spelling in the 1800s.
namesakes: Jennie Kim (Blackpink singer known as Jennie)

e.meaning: form of Gervase; perhaps spear servant
e.etymology: From an English surname that grew out of a Middle English form of Gervase, a Norman name whose first element is Germanic ger, 'spear'; the rest is uncertain.

assoc.t: J.A.R.V.I.S., Tony Stark's AI in the Marvel films

e.etymology: An African American coinage that adds the De- prefix to Marcus, the Roman name linked to the god Mars. It spread in the 1970s through the 1990s with Deandre and Demario.
namesakes: DeMarcus Ware (Hall of Fame NFL pass rusher)

e.etymology: A modern spelling of Cameron, the Scottish clan surname from Gaelic cam, 'crooked', and sron, 'nose'.
From the district of west London, named in Domesday Book: the Old English personal name Cynesige plus -ing- and tun, 'estate'. American parents began using it for girls in the 2000s.

assoc.t: Kensington, upscale district of west London
Kensington laptop locks and computer accessories

e.etymology: From a surname carried by old New England families. It was a first name in 19th-century America and has returned alongside Hayes and Hayden.
From Arabic aziz, which means both 'mighty, powerful' and 'dear, precious'. Al-Aziz, 'the Almighty', is one of the names of God in Islam, so the name also appears as Abdul Aziz.
namesakes: Aziz Ansari (comedian and Parks and Recreation actor)

e.etymology: A pet form of Katherine, from Greek Aikaterine. The original meaning is uncertain, but early Christians tied it to Greek katharos, 'pure', and that sense has stuck.

The Spanish and Portuguese spelling of Priscilla, a diminutive of the Roman family name Priscus, from Latin priscus, 'ancient, of old'. In the New Testament Priscilla is a friend and co-worker of Paul.
A short form of Maria in Dutch, German and English. Many American bearers are of Indian descent, for whom Ria is a spelling of Riya; it is also an Indonesian name from a word for joyful.

e.meaning: lord, ruler; a name of Shiva
e.etymology: From Sanskrit ishana, 'ruling, lord', an epithet of the god Shiva and the name of the guardian of the northeast direction.
It matches an English surname, a variant of Heasley, but as a girls' name it is a 2020s creation that joins the sound of Hazel to the -ley of Hadley and Paisley.
A blend of Emely or Emily with the -lyn ending, also used as a short spelling of Emmeline, an old Norman name built on the Germanic element amal, 'work'.
From Arabic huda, 'guidance', a word the Quran uses for divine guidance. It is a long-established girls' name across the Arab world.
namesakes: Huda Kattan (makeup artist who founded Huda Beauty)

e.etymology: A double-n spelling of Diana, the Roman goddess of the hunt and the moon, whose name comes from an old Italic root meaning divine or shining.

assoc.t: Diana, Princess of Wales (spelled with one n)

e.meaning: little pale one (Irish), or pine tree (Hebrew)
e.etymology: An anglicized spelling of Irish Odhran, a saint's name from odhar, 'dun, sallow'. It can also be a variant of Hebrew Oren, 'pine tree'. Orin and Orrin were common in 19th-century America.
namesakes: Orin Scrivello (the dentist in Little Shop of Horrors)
